Yeah — three is the real threshold, not two, so this is exactly the case for it, not premature.

One thing to check before extracting though: are all three actually the same shape, or just superficially similar? Specifically:

- Same backoff curve (exponential base, jitter or not, max delay)?
- Same retry predicate (retry on any exception, or only specific ones — timeouts vs. 5xxs vs. connection resets)?
- Same max-attempts, and does that number need to vary by call site?

If those line up, pull it into a small helper (`retry_with_backoff(fn, max_attempts, base_delay, retryable_check)` or similar) and swap all three over. If one of them is actually retrying on a different condition or needs a different backoff curve, don't force it into the same helper just because the syntax looks similar — that's how you get a "shared" function with three boolean flags bolted on to handle each caller's special case, which is worse than the duplication.

Have you looked at the three sites side by side, or just noticed the pattern repeating? If you haven't diffed them yet, that's worth doing before writing the helper — otherwise we're guessing at the shape.
